name: Centro Historico
tagline: The neocolonial centre and its thirty churches
description: La Serena's centre, rebuilt in a neocolonial style through a twentieth-century restoration programme that gave it a coherent stone look and around thirty churches. The Plaza de Armas, the archaeological museum with its Easter Island moai and the market are all here, four kilometres inland from the beach.
bestFor: Anyone who wants the plazas, the churches and the market on foot
pros: Plaza de Armas and the churches within a short walk
Market, museums and services all central
Cooler and less windy than the seafront
cons: Quiet in the evening outside summer

name: Avenida del Mar
tagline: The beachfront strip, apartments and the lighthouse
description: The six-kilometre avenue running along the beach between La Serena and Coquimbo, lined with apartment towers, restaurants and the red and white lighthouse that is the city's emblem. It fills with Chilean holidaymakers in January and February and is quiet the rest of the year.
bestFor: Summer stays that want the beach directly outside
pros: Long beach and the promenade at the door
The lighthouse and the seafront restaurants
Sea air and cooler summer temperatures
cons: Rents peak sharply in January and February
Windy and often foggy in the mornings

name: Coquimbo
tagline: The working port next door, rougher and cheaper
description: The separate city four kilometres south, built around a working fishing and container port with the Barrio Ingles of restored nineteenth-century buildings, the enormous Cruz del Tercer Milenio on the hill and a livelier evening scene than La Serena. Rents are lower and the character is more robust.
bestFor: Longer stays wanting lower rents and a livelier evening
pros: Cheaper than La Serena for equivalent housing
The fish market and the Barrio Ingles
More going on in the evening
cons: Rougher, and requires more caution after dark
Less attractive than La Serena's centre

name: Las Compañias and the Inland Districts
tagline: Up the hill behind the city, where the value is
description: The residential districts climbing the hill north and east of the centre, with ordinary Chilean housing, local shops and schools, and no view of anything in particular. Rents here are the lowest in the conurbation, and the centre is a short bus or colectivo ride downhill.
bestFor: Long stays where the rent is the deciding factor
pros: The lowest rents in the area
Local shops and markets at ordinary prices
cons: No sea view and no atmosphere
Fifteen to twenty minutes into the centre

name: Elqui Valley (60 km east)
tagline: The pisco valley and the observatory skies
description: The valley climbing east into the Andes through vineyards, pisco distilleries and small villages like Vicuna and Pisco Elqui, under skies clear enough that several international observatories are sited on the ridges above. The stargazing is genuinely world class and the valley has a long mystic reputation.
bestFor: Stays organised around the observatories and the valley rather than the coast
pros: Among the clearest night skies in the world
Pisco distilleries and vineyards along the valley
Warm, dry and sunny when the coast is foggy
cons: An hour from La Serena and a car is needed
Very limited services in the villages
Small villages with little going on
